caption:
Comment BLUEPRINT and I'll send it over: the whole faceless model, written out.

An hour of driving pays for one hour. An hour of delivery pays for one hour. That's the deal with almost every hourly gig. Your time goes in, its worth comes out, then it resets to zero.

THE HOUR THAT DOESN'T RESET

A post works differently. You spend the hour once, writing or recording it. After that it stays live. It can get seen, and can earn, whether you're driving, sleeping, or off the clock completely. The hour and the payout stop being the same thing.

HOW

You make the post once. It stays live, no new shift to clock into. It can earn on repeat: this week, next month, whenever someone sees it and buys through it.

THE HONEST PART

This isn't a claim about what you'll make. An hourly gig has a hard ceiling: hours in a day, times the rate. A post doesn't have that ceiling. Whether it earns anything still depends on you actually making it, and making more than one.

It could be zero. Post once and stop, and it's zero. This is math about which one has a ceiling, not a promise about results.
